summary.text: A 79-year-old woman presented to an otorhinolaryngology outpatient clinic with a one-month history of right facial palsy, vertigo, dizziness, right postauricular pain and right-sided hearing disturbance. Examination showed marked right peripheral facial palsy (House-Brackmann grade IV), gaze-evoked nystagmus and cerebellar ataxic gait, without a significant facial sensory deficit. Her history included hip and knee arthroplasties in 2017 and no neurological, psychological or metabolic disorders.

Brain MRI showed a 3.4 × 2.7 cm solid cystic mass in the right cerebellopontine angle and internal auditory canal, distorting the brainstem, narrowing the fourth ventricle and causing mild obstructive hydrocephalus. She was referred for electrodiagnostic analysis. Facial nerve conduction showed delayed latency (except in orbicularis oculi) and small amplitudes on the right, blink reflex testing showed absent right-sided responses, and needle EMG showed right-sided abnormal spontaneous activity, confirming trigeminal and facial nerve injury with subacute axonal loss.

One week later she underwent retromastoid suboccipital craniotomy for tumor excision; the tumor grossly compressed the trigeminal and facial nerves, there were no postoperative complications, histopathology confirmed vestibular schwannoma, and neurologic symptoms partially improved. A brain MRI one month after surgery showed a remnant tumor mass near the right internal auditory canal, treated with additional gamma knife radiosurgery.
One month after gamma knife radiosurgery the patient showed recovery from the right facial palsy, to House-Brackmann grade II.
